literal: Paul, a slave of Jesus Christ, a called apostle, having been set apart unto the gospel of God,
prose: Paul, a servant of Jesus Christ, called an apostle, set apart for the gospel of God,

literal: which He promised beforehand through His prophets in holy scriptures
prose: which He promised beforehand through His prophets in the holy scriptures

literal: concerning his Son, the one having come of the seed of David according to flesh,
prose: concerning his Son, who was born of the seed of David according to the flesh,

literal: the one having been marked out [as] Son of God in power according to [the] spirit of holiness from resurrection of dead ones, of Jesus Christ our Lord,
prose: who was declared Son of God in power, according to the spirit of holiness, by resurrection from the dead—Jesus Christ our Lord,

literal: through whom we received grace and apostleship unto obedience of faith among all the nations, on behalf of his name,
prose: through whom we received grace and apostleship for obedience of faith among all the nations, on behalf of his name,

literal: among whom you also are called ones of Jesus Christ,
prose: among whom you also are called of Jesus Christ,

literal: To all those being in Rome, beloved of God, called holy ones: grace to you and peace from God [our] Father of us and of Lord Jesus Christ.
prose: To all who are in Rome, beloved of God, called saints: grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.

literal: First indeed I thank the God of me through Jesus Christ concerning all of you, because the faith of you is proclaimed in [the] whole world.
prose: First of all, I thank my God through Jesus Christ for all of you, because your faith is proclaimed throughout the whole world.

literal: For witness of me is God, to whom I render service in the spirit of me in the gospel of the Son of him, how unceasingly mention of you I make,
prose: For God, whom I serve with my spirit in the gospel of his Son, is my witness that I constantly make mention of you,

literal: always at the prayers of me, asking if somehow now at last I shall be prospered, in the will of God, to come to you.
prose: always in my prayers, asking that somehow, at last, I may now succeed by God's will in coming to you.

literal: For I long to see you, in order that I might impart some spiritual gift to you, unto the strengthening of you,
prose: For I long to see you, so that I may share some spiritual gift with you, for your strengthening,

literal: And this is, to be mutually encouraged among you, through the faith of one another, both of you and of me.
prose: That is, that we may be mutually encouraged among you through the faith that is in one another, both yours and mine.

literal: Not I want but you to be ignorant, brothers, that many times I purposed to come to you, and was prevented until the now, in order that some fruit I might have also in you, just as also in the rest [to the] nations.
prose: I do not want you to be unaware, brothers, that many times I intended to come to you, but was prevented until now, so that I might have some fruit among you also, just as also among the rest of the Gentiles.

literal: To Greeks both and to barbarians, to wise both and to foolish, a debtor I am;
prose: I am a debtor both to Greeks and to barbarians, both to the wise and to the foolish.

literal: So the [part] according to me [is] eager also to you, the [ones] in Rome, to preach the gospel.
prose: So, as far as I am concerned, I am eager to preach the gospel to you also who are in Rome.

literal: For not I am ashamed of the gospel, for [it] is power of God unto salvation to everyone who believes, to Jew both [first] and to Greek.
prose: For I am not ashamed of the gospel, since it is the power of God for salvation to everyone who believes, to the Jew first and also to the Greek.

literal: For [the] righteousness of God in it is revealed, from faith to faith, as it has been written: The [one] but righteous by faith will live.
prose: For in it the righteousness of God is revealed, from faith to faith, as it is written: "The righteous one will live by faith."

literal: For is being revealed wrath of God from heaven upon all ungodliness and wickedness of men, of those the truth in wickedness suppressing,
prose: For the wrath of God is being revealed from heaven against all the ungodliness and wickedness of men who suppress the truth in wickedness,

literal: Because the known-thing of God plain is among them; for God to them made [it] plain.
prose: Because what can be known of God is plain among them, for God has made it plain to them.

literal: For the invisible things of him, from [the] creation of [the] world, by the things made being perceived, are clearly seen, both his eternal power and divinity, unto their being without excuse,
prose: For his invisible qualities—his eternal power and divinity—have been clearly seen ever since the creation of the world, being understood through the things he has made, so that they are without excuse,

literal: because, having known God, not as God did they glorify [him] or give thanks, but they were made vain in their reasonings, and was darkened their senseless heart.
prose: because, although they knew God, they did not glorify him as God or give him thanks, but became futile in their reasonings, and their senseless hearts were darkened.

literal: Claiming to be wise, they were made foolish,
prose: Claiming to be wise, they became fools,

literal: And they exchanged the glory of the incorruptible God in a likeness of an image of corruptible man, and of birds, and of four-footed animals, and of reptiles.
prose: And they exchanged the glory of the incorruptible God for an image made in the likeness of corruptible man, and of birds, and of four-footed animals, and of reptiles.

literal: Therefore handed over them the God, in the desires of the hearts of them, unto uncleanness, of the being dishonored the bodies of them among themselves,
prose: Therefore God gave them over, in the desires of their hearts, to impurity, so that their bodies were dishonored among themselves,

literal: who exchanged the truth of God for the lie, and worshipped and served the creation beside the one who created [it], who is blessed unto the ages; Amen.
prose: They exchanged the truth of God for a lie, and worshipped and served the creation rather than the Creator, who is blessed forever. Amen.

literal: For their females exchanged the natural use into that which is contrary to nature,
prose: For their women exchanged natural relations for what is contrary to nature,

literal: And likewise also the males, having abandoned the natural use of the female, were inflamed in their desire toward one another, males with males working out the shamelessness, and receiving back in themselves the recompense which was necessary of their error.
prose: Likewise the men too, abandoning natural relations with women, were inflamed with lust for one another, men committing shameless acts with men, and receiving in themselves the due penalty for their error.

literal: And just as they did not approve to have God in [full] knowledge, God gave them over to a debased mind, to do the things not proper,
prose: And just as they did not see fit to acknowledge God, God gave them over to a debased mind, to do the things that are not proper,

literal: having been filled with all unrighteousness, wickedness, greed, malice; full of envy, murder, strife, deceit, depravity; whisperers,
prose: filled with all unrighteousness, wickedness, greed, malice; full of envy, murder, strife, deceit, depravity; whisperers,

literal: slanderers, God-haters, insolent [ones], arrogant [ones], boasters, inventors of evils, disobedient to parents, senseless,
prose: slanderers, haters of God, insolent, arrogant, boastful, inventors of evil things, disobedient to parents, senseless,

literal: Faithless [ones], unloving [ones], unmerciful [ones];
prose: Faithless, unloving, unmerciful.

literal: Who, having known the decree of God, that those practicing such things are worthy of death, not only do them, but also approve of those practicing [them].
prose: Though they know God's decree—that those who practice such things deserve death—they not only do them themselves but also approve of those who practice them.

literal: Therefore without-excuse you-are, O man, every [one] the [one] judging; for in that in which you judge the other, yourself you-condemn, for the same things you-practice, the [one] judging.
prose: Therefore you are without excuse, O man—every one of you who judges. For in that in which you judge the other person, you condemn yourself; for you who judge practice the same things.

literal: that the judgment of God is according to truth upon those practicing such things
prose: that God's judgment is according to truth upon those who practice such things

literal: But do you reckon this, O man, the one judging those practicing such things and doing them yourself, that you will escape the judgment of God?
prose: Do you reckon this, O man who judges those who practice such things and yet do them yourself, that you will escape the judgment of God?

literal: Or of-the riches of-the kindness of-him and of-the forbearance and of-the patience you-despise, not-knowing that the kindness of-the God into repentance you it-leads?
prose: Or do you despise the riches of his kindness and forbearance and patience, not knowing that the kindness of God is leading you to repentance?

literal: But according to your hardness and unrepentant heart you store up for yourself wrath, in a day of wrath and of revelation of righteous judgment of God,
prose: But because of your hardness and unrepentant heart you are storing up wrath for yourself on the day of wrath and revelation of the righteous judgment of God,

literal: who will render to each one according to his works:
prose: who will render to each one according to his works:

literal: to the [ones] on the one hand according to endurance of good work glory and honor and incorruptibility seeking, eternal life;
prose: to those who seek glory and honor and immortality by perseverance in good work, eternal life;

literal: but to-those out-of contentiousness and disobeying the truth, but obeying unrighteousness—wrath and fury,
prose: but to those who are out of contentiousness and disobey the truth, but obey unrighteousness—wrath and fury,

literal: affliction and distress, upon every soul of-man of-the-one working-out the evil, of-Jew both first and of-Greek;
prose: affliction and distress, upon every soul of man who works out evil, of Jew first and also of Greek;

literal: But glory and honor and peace to everyone the [one] working the good, to Jew both first and to Greek;
prose: But glory and honor and peace to everyone who works what is good, to the Jew first and also to the Greek;

literal: For there is not partiality with God.
prose: For there is no partiality with God.

literal: For as many as sinned without law, without law also will perish; and as many as sinned in [the] law, through [the] law will be judged;
prose: For as many as have sinned without the law will also perish without the law; and as many as have sinned within the law will be judged by the law;

literal: For not the hearers of law [are] righteous before [the] God, but the doers of law will be justified.
prose: For it is not the hearers of law who are righteous before God, but the doers of law will be justified.

literal: For whenever Gentiles, the ones not having law, by nature do the things of the law, these, not having law, are law to themselves;
prose: For when Gentiles, who do not have the law, do by nature the things of the law, these, though not having the law, are a law to themselves;

literal: who show the work of the law [to be] written in their hearts, their conscience bearing-witness-with [them], and between one another their thoughts accusing or also defending [them],
prose: who show that the work of the law is written in their hearts, their conscience bearing joint witness, and their thoughts between one another accusing or even defending them,

literal: in which day God judges the hidden things of men according to my gospel through Christ Jesus
prose: on the day when God judges the hidden things of men according to my gospel through Christ Jesus

literal: If but you a Jew are named, and rest upon [the] law, and boast in God,
prose: But if you call yourself a Jew, and rely on the law, and boast in God,

literal: and know the will [of him], and approve the things that differ, being instructed out of the law,
prose: and know his will, and approve the things that excel, being instructed out of the law,

literal: and have been persuaded [that] yourself a guide are of [the] blind, a light of those in darkness,
prose: and are persuaded that you yourself are a guide of the blind, a light of those in darkness,

literal: an instructor of [the] foolish, a teacher of infants, having the form of knowledge and of truth in the law —
prose: an instructor of the foolish, a teacher of infants, having in the law the embodiment of knowledge and of truth —

literal: The one preaching not to steal, do you steal?
prose: You who preach against stealing, do you steal?

literal: The one saying not to commit adultery, do you commit adultery? The one abhorring the idols, do you rob temples?
prose: You who say that one must not commit adultery—do you commit adultery? You who abhor idols, do you rob temples?

literal: You who in [the] law boast, through the transgression of the law do you dishonor God?
prose: You who boast in the law, do you dishonor God through your transgression of the law?

literal: For the name of God because of you is blasphemed among the Gentiles, just as it has been written.
prose: For the name of God is blasphemed among the Gentiles because of you, just as it is written.

literal: For circumcision indeed benefits, if you practice [the] law; if but a transgressor of law you are, the circumcision of you uncircumcision has become.
prose: For circumcision is indeed of benefit if you practice the law; but if you are a transgressor of the law, your circumcision has become uncircumcision.

literal: If then the uncircumcision should keep the righteous-requirements of the law, will not his uncircumcision be reckoned unto circumcision?
prose: If then the uncircumcision keeps the righteous requirements of the law, will not his uncircumcision be reckoned as circumcision?

literal: And will-judge the out-of nature uncircumcision the law fulfilling you, the through letter and circumcision transgressor of-law.
prose: And the uncircumcision that is by nature, if it fulfills the law, will judge you, who with letter and circumcision are a transgressor of the law.

literal: For not the [one] in the-outward [is] Jew is, nor the in the-outward in flesh circumcision [is];
prose: For it is not the one who is a Jew outwardly, nor is circumcision that which is outward in the flesh;

literal: But the [one] in the hidden [is] a Jew, and circumcision of heart in spirit, not in letter, of whom the praise [is] not from men but from God.
prose: But he is a Jew who is one inwardly, and circumcision is that of the heart, by the Spirit, not by the letter; his praise is not from men but from God.

literal: What then [is] the advantage of the Jew, or what [is] the benefit of circumcision?
prose: What advantage, then, does the Jew have, or what is the benefit of circumcision?

literal: Much according to every way. First indeed [for] because they were entrusted the oracles of the God.
prose: Much in every way; first of all, because they were entrusted with the oracles of God.

literal: For what? If some were unfaithful, will the unfaithfulness of them the faithfulness of God nullify?
prose: For what? If some were unfaithful, will their unfaithfulness nullify the faithfulness of God?

literal: But let God be true, and every man a liar, just as it has been written: "So that you might be justified in your words, and you will prevail in your being judged."
prose: But let God be true, and every man a liar, as it is written: "That you may be justified in your words, and may prevail when you are judged."

literal: But if our unrighteousness commends [the] righteousness of God, what shall we say? [Is] not unjust God, the one inflicting the wrath? According to man I speak.
prose: But if our unrighteousness commends the righteousness of God, what shall we say? Is God unjust to inflict wrath? I am speaking in human terms.

literal: May it not be! Since, how will God judge the world?
prose: Certainly not! Otherwise, how will God judge the world?

literal: But if the truth of God abounded in my falsehood to his glory, why am I still also, as a sinner, being judged,
prose: But if God's truth abounded through my falsehood to his glory, why am I still being judged as a sinner?

literal: And not as we are blasphemed, [and] as some say [that] we say, 'Let us do the evil things, in order that the good things may come'? Of whom the judgment just is.
prose: And why not say, as we are slanderously reported and as some claim we say, 'Let us do evil things so that good things may come'? Their condemnation is just.

literal: What then? Are we at an advantage? Not altogether, for we previously charged Jews both and Greeks all [that they] are under sin,
prose: What then? Are we at any advantage? Not at all; for we have already charged that Jews and Greeks alike are all under sin,

literal: just as it has been written, that: Not is [there] righteous, not even one; not is [there] understanding [one],
prose: as it is written: There is no righteous person, not even one; there is no one who understands;

literal: Not is [there] seeking-out the God.
prose: There is no one who seeks after God.

literal: All turned away, together they were made worthless; there is not [one] doing goodness, there is not [one] up to one.
prose: All turned away, together they became worthless; there is no one who does good, not even one.

literal: [The] throat [is] an opened [grave], the throat of them, with the tongues of them they were deceiving, venom of asps [is] under the lips of them,
prose: Their throat is an opened grave, with their tongues they kept deceiving, the venom of asps is under their lips,

literal: of whom the mouth of cursing and of bitterness is full;
prose: whose mouth is full of cursing and bitterness;

literal: Swift [are] the feet of them to shed blood,
prose: Their feet are swift to shed blood,

literal: ruin and misery [are] in their ways,
prose: ruin and misery are in their paths,

literal: and [the] way of peace they did not know.
prose: and the way of peace they have not known.

literal: There is not fear of God before the eyes of them.
prose: There is no fear of God before their eyes.

literal: But we know that as many things as the law says, it speaks to the [ones] in the law, in order that every mouth may be stopped and all the world may become liable-to-judgment to God;
prose: Now we know that whatever the law says, it speaks to those who are under the law, so that every mouth may be stopped and the whole world may become accountable to God;

literal: Because out-of works of-law not will-be-justified all flesh before Him, for through law [is] knowledge of-sin.
prose: Because by works of law no flesh will be justified before Him; for through law comes knowledge of sin.

literal: But now, apart from law, a righteousness of God has been manifested, being witnessed by the law and the prophets,
prose: But now, apart from law, the righteousness of God has been manifested, being witnessed to by the law and the prophets,

literal: and a righteousness of God through faith of [Jesus] Christ, unto all those believing, for there is not a distinction.
prose: the righteousness of God through faith in [Jesus] Christ, for all who believe; for there is no distinction.

literal: For all sinned and are falling short of the glory of the God,
prose: For all sinned and fall short of the glory of God,

literal: being justified freely by the his grace through the redemption, [the one] in Christ Jesus;
prose: being justified freely by his grace, through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus;

literal: whom God set forth [as] a mercy-seat, through faith, in his blood, for a demonstration of his righteousness, because of the passing-over of the sins having previously occurred
prose: whom God publicly set forth as a means of atonement, through faith, by his blood, to demonstrate his righteousness, because of the passing over of previously committed sins

literal: in the forbearance of God, for a demonstration of his righteousness in the now time, so that he [might] be just and justifying the [one] out of faith of Jesus.
prose: in God's forbearance, with a view to the demonstration of his righteousness at the present time, so that he might be just and the one who justifies the person who has faith in Jesus.

literal: Where then [is] the boasting? It was shut out. Through what kind of law [is it]? Of works [is it]? No, but through a law of faith [is it excluded].
prose: Where, then, is boasting? It was excluded. Through what kind of law? Of works? No, but through a law of faith.

literal: For we reckon [a] man to be justified by faith, apart from works of law.
prose: For we conclude that a person is justified by faith, apart from works of the law.

literal: Or [is] the God of Jews only? [Is he] not also [God] of Gentiles?
prose: Or is God the God of Jews only? Is he not also God of Gentiles?

literal: Yes, also of Gentiles, since [he is] one, God, who will justify circumcision from faith and uncircumcision through the faith.
prose: Yes, of Gentiles too, since God is one, who will justify the circumcised by faith and the uncircumcised through their faith.

literal: May it not be, but law we uphold.
prose: By no means! Rather, we uphold the law.

literal: What then shall we say Abraham our forefather according to flesh [found]?
prose: What then shall we say that Abraham, our forefather according to the flesh, found?

literal: For if Abraham was justified out of works, he has a boast; but not toward God, for what does the scripture say?
prose: For if Abraham was justified by works, he has a ground for boasting—but not with reference to God. For what does the scripture say?

literal: And Abraham believed God, and it was credited to him unto righteousness.
prose: And Abraham believed God, and it was credited to him as righteousness.

literal: But to the one working, the wage is not reckoned according to grace, but according to debt.
prose: Now to the one who works, the wages are not reckoned as a favor, but as a debt owed.

literal: But to the one not working, but believing on the one justifying the ungodly, his faith is credited unto righteousness,
prose: But to the one who does not work, but believes on him who justifies the ungodly, his faith is credited as righteousness,

literal: just as also David speaks the blessing of the man to whom God credits righteousness apart from works,
prose: just as David also speaks of the blessing of the man to whom God credits righteousness apart from works,

literal: Blessed [are they] of whom the lawless deeds were forgiven, and of whom the sins were covered,
prose: "Blessed are they whose lawless deeds have been forgiven, and whose sins have been covered,"

literal: blessed [is the] man of whom the Lord shall by no means credit sin.
prose: blessed is the man against whom the Lord will by no means credit sin.

literal: This blessing, therefore, [is it] upon the circumcision, or also upon the uncircumcision? For we say: "Faith was credited to [the] Abraham unto righteousness."
prose: Is this blessing, then, upon the circumcision, or also upon the uncircumcision? For we say, "Faith was credited to Abraham as righteousness."

literal: How then was it reckoned? [Was it reckoned] while being in circumcision, or in uncircumcision? Not in circumcision, but in uncircumcision — [it was reckoned].
prose: How then was it reckoned? Was it while he was circumcised, or uncircumcised? Not while circumcised, but while uncircumcised.

literal: And a sign he received, of circumcision, a seal of the righteousness of the faith which [was] in uncircumcision, for him to be the father of all those believing through uncircumcision, for righteousness to be reckoned to them,
prose: And he received circumcision as a sign, a seal of the righteousness that came through the faith he had while uncircumcised, so that he might be the father of all who believe while uncircumcised, in order that righteousness might be credited to them as well,

literal: and a father of circumcision to those not of circumcision only but also to those walking in the footsteps of the faith in uncircumcision of our father Abraham.
prose: and the father of circumcision to those who are not only of the circumcision but who also follow in the footsteps of the faith which our father Abraham had while uncircumcised.

literal: For not through law [was] the promise to Abraham or to his descendant, that he be heir of the world, but through the righteousness of faith.
prose: For it was not through law that the promise came to Abraham or to his descendant that he would be heir of the world, but through the righteousness of faith.

literal: For if those [who are] of [the] law [are] heirs, faith has been emptied, and the promise has been nullified.
prose: For if those who are of the law are heirs, faith has been emptied, and the promise has been nullified.

literal: For the law wrath works-out, but where law is not, neither transgression.
prose: For the law brings about wrath; but where there is no law, there is no transgression either.

literal: Because of this, [it is] from faith, in order that [it may be] according to grace, for the promise to be sure to all the seed, not to that from the law only, but also to that from the faith of Abraham (who is father of all of us, just as it has been written, that, 'A father of many nations I have made you'),
prose: Therefore it is by faith, so that it may be according to grace, in order that the promise may be guaranteed to all the offspring—not only to the offspring who are of the law, but also to the offspring who are of the faith of Abraham (who is the father of us all, as it is written, "I have made you a father of many nations"),

literal: just as it has been written, that, 'A father of many nations I have made you'—before whom he believed—of God, the one giving life to the dead and calling the things not existing as existing.
prose: as it is written, 'I have made you a father of many nations'—before God, in whose presence he believed, the God who gives life to the dead and calls the things that do not exist as though they existed.

literal: Who against hope, in hope, believed, for him to become father of many nations, according to the thing having been said, "Thus shall be the seed of you";
prose: Who, against hope, believed in hope, so that he became the father of many nations, according to what had been said, "So shall your offspring be";

literal: And not having weakened in the faith, he considered his own body, [already] having been deadened already, being about a hundred years old, and the deadening of the womb of Sarah,
prose: And without weakening in faith, he considered his own body, already dead, since he was about a hundred years old, and the deadness of Sarah's womb,

literal: But with regard to the promise of God he did not waver in unbelief, but was strengthened in faith, having given glory to God,
prose: Yet regarding the promise of God, he did not waver in unbelief, but was strengthened in faith, giving glory to God,

literal: and having been fully convinced that what He has promised, He is able also to do.
prose: and being fully convinced that what He had promised, He was able also to do.

literal: Therefore [also] it was credited to him unto righteousness.
prose: Therefore it was also credited to him as righteousness.

literal: Not but it-was-written for-his-sake only, that it-was-credited to-him,
prose: Now it was not written for his sake alone that it was credited to him,

literal: but also for-our-sake, to-whom it-is-about to-be-credited, to-the ones-believing upon the one-having-raised Jesus the Lord of-us out-of dead-ones,
prose: but also for our sake, to whom it is going to be credited, who believe on him who raised Jesus our Lord from the dead,

literal: who was-handed-over because-of the transgressions of-us and was-raised because-of the justification of-us.
prose: who was handed over because of our transgressions and was raised because of our justification.

literal: Having been justified, therefore, from faith, let us have peace toward God through our Lord Jesus Christ,
prose: Therefore, having been justified by faith, let us have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ,

literal: through whom also we have obtained the access [by faith] into this grace in which we have stood, and let us boast upon hope of the glory of God;
prose: through whom also we have obtained our access [by faith] into this grace in which we stand, and let us boast in hope of the glory of God;

literal: Not only [so], but also we boast in the afflictions, knowing that the affliction produces endurance,
prose: And not only that, but we also boast in our afflictions, knowing that affliction produces endurance,

literal: and the endurance [produces] proven character, and the proven character [produces] hope,
prose: and endurance produces proven character, and proven character produces hope,

literal: because the love of God has been poured out in our hearts through [the] Spirit holy, the one having been given to us;
prose: because the love of God has been poured out in our hearts through the Holy Spirit who was given to us;

literal: For if indeed, while we were still weak, Christ, at the time, for the ungodly, died.
prose: For while we were still weak, Christ died at the appointed time for the ungodly.

literal: For on behalf of the good [man], perhaps someone even dares to die.
prose: For on behalf of the good man, perhaps someone even dares to die.

literal: But God demonstrates his own love toward us, in that while we were still sinners, Christ died on behalf of us.
prose: But God demonstrates his own love toward us, in that while we were still sinners, Christ died on our behalf.

literal: By much then more, having been justified now in the blood of him, we will be saved through him from the wrath.
prose: Much more then, having now been justified by his blood, we will be saved through him from the wrath.

literal: For if, being enemies, we were reconciled to God through the death of his Son, much more, having been reconciled, we will be saved in his life.
prose: For if, while we were enemies, we were reconciled to God through the death of his Son, much more, having been reconciled, we shall be saved by his life.

literal: Not only [so], but also boasting in God through our Lord Jesus [Christ], through whom now the reconciliation we received.
prose: Not only so, but we also boast in God through our Lord Jesus Christ, through whom we have now received the reconciliation.

literal: Through this, just as through one man sin entered into the world, and through sin death, and thus also death spread to all men, upon which all sinned.
prose: Therefore, just as sin entered into the world through one man, and death through sin, so also death spread to all men, because all sinned.

literal: For until law, sin was in [the] world, but sin is not counted [when] law is not being,
prose: For until the law, sin was in the world, but sin is not counted where there is no law,

literal: But death reigned from Adam until Moses, even upon those not having sinned upon the likeness of the transgression of Adam, who is a type of the [one] about to be [coming].
prose: But death reigned from Adam until Moses, even over those who had not sinned in the likeness of Adam's transgression, who is a type of the one who was to come.

literal: For if by the trespass of the one [man] the many died, by much more the grace of God and the gift in grace, [that] of the one man Jesus Christ, abounded unto the many.
prose: For if by the trespass of the one man the many died, much more did the grace of God and the gift in grace, that of the one man Jesus Christ, abound to the many.

literal: For the judgment on the one hand [came] from one [trespass] unto condemnation, but the gift on the other hand [came] from many trespasses unto righteousness.
prose: For on the one hand the judgment from one trespass led to condemnation, but on the other hand the gift from many trespasses led to righteousness.

literal: For if by the trespass of the one, death reigned through the one, much more those receiving the abundance of grace and [of the gift] of righteousness will reign in life through the one, Jesus Christ.
prose: For if by the trespass of the one man death reigned through that one man, much more will those who receive the abundance of grace and of the gift of righteousness reign in life through the one man, Jesus Christ.

literal: So then, as through one trespass to all men to condemnation, thus also through one righteous act to all men to justification of life;
prose: So then, as through one trespass [the result came] to all men, to condemnation, so also through one righteous act [the result came] to all men, to justification of life;

literal: For just as through the disobedience of the one man the many were constituted sinners, so also through the obedience of the one the many will be constituted righteous.
prose: For just as through the disobedience of the one man the many were made sinners, so also through the obedience of the one the many will be made righteous.

literal: Now law came in alongside, in order that the trespass might increase; but where sin increased, grace increased-beyond,
prose: Now law came in alongside, so that the trespass might increase; but where sin increased, grace increased all the more,

literal: in order that, just as sin reigned in death, so also grace might reign through righteousness unto eternal life through Jesus Christ the Lord of us.
prose: so that just as sin reigned in death, so also grace might reign through righteousness unto eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord.

literal: What then shall we say? Should we continue in sin, in order that the grace may increase?
prose: What then shall we say? Should we continue in sin, so that grace may increase?

literal: May it not be! We who died to the sin, how shall we still live in it?
prose: Certainly not! We who died to sin—how shall we still live in it?

literal: Or do you not know that as many of us as were baptized into Christ [Jesus] were baptized into his death?
prose: Or do you not know that all of us who were baptized into Christ Jesus were baptized into his death?

literal: We were buried together, therefore, with him through the baptism into the death, so that just as Christ was raised from dead ones through the glory of the Father, so also we might walk in newness of life.
prose: We were therefore buried with him through baptism into death, so that just as Christ was raised from the dead through the glory of the Father, so we also might walk in newness of life.

literal: For if we have become co-planted [united-growing] to the likeness of his death, but also of the resurrection we shall be;
prose: For if we have become united with him in the likeness of his death, we shall certainly also be united with him in the likeness of his resurrection;

literal: This knowing, that the old man of us was crucified-with [him], in order that the body of sin might be rendered inoperative, [in order] for us no longer to be enslaved to sin,
prose: Knowing this, that our old self was crucified with him, so that the body of sin might be rendered powerless, so that we should no longer be enslaved to sin;

literal: For the one having died has been justified from sin.
prose: For the one who has died has been justified from sin.

literal: But if we died with Christ, we believe that we will also live together with him.
prose: But if we died with Christ, we believe that we will also live with him.

literal: Knowing that Christ, having been raised from [the] dead, no longer dies; death no longer lords [it] over him;
prose: Knowing that Christ, having been raised from the dead, no longer dies; death no longer has dominion over him.

literal: For that which he died, he died to sin once for all;
prose: For the death he died, he died to sin once for all,

literal: Thus also you(pl) consider yourselves to be dead on the one hand to sin, but living to God in Christ Jesus.
prose: So you also must consider yourselves to be dead to sin, but alive to God in Christ Jesus.

literal: Let not therefore sin reign in your mortal body, with a view to obeying its desires,
prose: Therefore do not let sin reign in your mortal body, so that you obey its desires,

literal: and do not present your members to sin as weapons of unrighteousness, but present yourselves to God as alive out of dead [ones], and your members [present] to God as weapons of righteousness;
prose: and do not present your members to sin as weapons of unrighteousness, but present yourselves to God as alive from the dead, and your members to God as weapons of righteousness;

literal: For sin over you shall not be lord, for you are not under law but under grace.
prose: For sin shall not have dominion over you, since you are not under law but under grace.

literal: What then [shall we say]? Shall we sin, because we are not under law but under grace? Let it not be!
prose: What then? Shall we sin, because we are not under law but under grace? By no means!

literal: Do you not know that to whom you present yourselves slaves for obedience, slaves you are to whom you obey, whether of sin unto death, or of obedience unto righteousness?
prose: Do you not know that to whomever you present yourselves as slaves for obedience, you are slaves of the one whom you obey, whether of sin leading to death, or of obedience leading to righteousness?

literal: But thanks [be] to God, that you were slaves of sin, but you obeyed from [the] heart [the] pattern of teaching to which you were handed over,
prose: But thanks be to God that, though you were slaves of sin, you obeyed from the heart the pattern of teaching to which you were handed over,

literal: And having been freed from sin, you were enslaved to righteousness.
prose: And having been freed from sin, you became slaves to righteousness.

literal: [A] human [thing] I speak, because of the weakness of the flesh of you.
prose: I speak in human terms because of the weakness of your flesh.

literal: For when you were slaves of sin, you were free to righteousness.
prose: For when you were slaves of sin, you were free with regard to righteousness.

literal: What then fruit were you having then from [the] things in which now you are ashamed? For the end of those [things] [is] death.
prose: What fruit, then, did you have at that time from the things you are now ashamed of? For the end of those things is death.

literal: But now, having been freed from sin and having been enslaved to God, you have the fruit of you unto sanctification, and the end, eternal life.
prose: But now, having been freed from sin and enslaved to God, you have your fruit leading to sanctification, and the end, eternal life.

literal: For the wages of sin [are] death, but the gift of God [is] eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord.
prose: For the wages of sin are death, but the free gift of God is eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord.

literal: Or do you not know, brothers (for to [those] knowing law I am speaking), that the law has-lordship-over the man for as much time as he lives?
prose: Or do you not know, brothers—for I am speaking to those who know law—that the law has authority over a person for as long as he lives?

literal: For the woman-with-a-husband to-the living husband is-bound by-law; but if the husband dies, she-has-been-discharged from the law of-the husband.
prose: For the married woman is bound by law to her living husband; but if the husband dies, she is released from the law of the husband.

literal: Accordingly then, the husband living, she will be called an adulteress, if she becomes [wife] to another husband; but if the husband should die, she is free from the law, of her not being an adulteress, having become [wife] to another husband.
prose: So then, while her husband is living, she will be called an adulteress if she becomes another man's wife; but if the husband dies, she is free from the law, so that she is not an adulteress by becoming another man's wife.

literal: So that, my brothers of me, you too were put to death to the law through the body of the Christ, for you to become to another, to the one raised from the dead, in order that we might bear fruit to God.
prose: So then, my brothers, you too were put to death to the law through the body of Christ, so that you might belong to another, to him who was raised from the dead, in order that we might bear fruit for God.

literal: For when we were in the flesh, the passions of sins, those through the law, were working in our members unto the bearing of fruit for death;
prose: For when we were in the flesh, the sinful passions that worked through the law were at work in our members to bear fruit for death.

literal: But now we were discharged from the law, having died in that in which we were held, so that we serve in newness of spirit and not in oldness of letter.
prose: But now we have been released from the law, having died to that in which we were held, so that we serve in newness of spirit and not in oldness of letter.

literal: What then shall we say? [Is] the law sin? May it not be! But sin I did not know, except through law; for indeed covetousness I would not have known, except the law said, "You shall not covet";
prose: What then shall we say? Is the law sin? Certainly not! Rather, I would not have known sin except through the law; for indeed I would not have known covetousness, unless the law had said, "You shall not covet."

literal: But sin, having taken an opportunity through the commandment, worked out in me every desire; for apart from law sin [is] dead.
prose: But sin, seizing an opportunity through the commandment, produced in me every kind of desire; for apart from law, sin is dead.

literal: I but was living apart from law once. But the commandment having come, sin lived again,
prose: But I was once alive apart from the law. But when the commandment came, sin sprang to life,

literal: and I died, and the commandment, the one for life, this one was found by me to be for death;
prose: and I died; and the commandment that was meant for life proved, for me, to result in death;

literal: For sin, having taken opportunity through the commandment, deceived me, and through it killed [me].
prose: For sin, seizing an opportunity through the commandment, deceived me, and through it killed me.

literal: So-that the law on the one hand [is] holy, and the commandment [is] holy and just and good.
prose: So the law is holy, and the commandment is holy and just and good.

literal: The good, then, to me, did it become death? May it not be! But sin [it was], in order that sin might appear sin, through the good working out for me death; in order that it might become, according to excess, sinful — sin — through the commandment.
prose: Did, then, what is good become death to me? Certainly not! But it was sin, so that sin might appear sin, working out death for me through what was good, so that sin might become sinful beyond measure through the commandment.

literal: For we know that the law is spiritual; but I am fleshly, having been sold under the sin.
prose: For we know that the law is spiritual; but I am made of flesh, sold under sin.

literal: For what I work, I do not know; for not what I will, this I practice, but what I hate, this I do.
prose: For what I do, I do not understand; for what I will, this I do not practice, but what I hate, this I do.

literal: But if what I do not want, this I do, I agree with the law, that [it is] good.
prose: But if I do what I do not want, I agree with the law that it is good.

literal: But now no longer I work out it, but the sin dwelling in me [works it out].
prose: But now it is no longer I who do it, but the sin dwelling in me.

literal: For I-know that [it] does-not dwell in me — this is, in the flesh of-me — good; for the to-will is-present to-me, but the to-accomplish the good [is] not.
prose: For I know that nothing good dwells in me, that is, in my flesh; for to will is present with me, but to accomplish the good is not.

literal: For not what I want, I do, good, but what I do not want, this, evil, I practice.
prose: For I do not do the good that I want, but the evil that I do not want—this I practice.

literal: But if what I do not want, this I do, no longer I work it, but the sin dwelling in me [works it].
prose: But if I do what I do not want, it is no longer I who do it, but the sin that dwells in me.

literal: I find, then, the law for me who wants to do the good, that for me evil lies close at hand.
prose: So I find this law: that for me, who wants to do good, evil lies close at hand.

literal: For I delight in the law of God according to the inner man,
prose: For I delight in the law of God according to the inner man,

literal: but I see another law in my members, warring against the law of my mind and taking captive me [in] the law of sin that is in my members
prose: but I see another law in my members, warring against the law of my mind and taking me captive to the law of sin that is in my members

literal: Wretched I [am] [a] man; who will rescue me out of the body of this death?
prose: Wretched man that I am! Who will rescue me from this body of death?

literal: But thanks [be] to God through Jesus Christ our Lord.
prose: But thanks be to God through Jesus Christ our Lord.

literal: Nothing, then, now [as] condemnation for those [who are] in Christ Jesus.
prose: There is, then, now no condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus.

literal: For the law of the Spirit of the life in Christ Jesus freed you from the law of sin and of death.
prose: For the law of the Spirit of life in Christ Jesus freed you from the law of sin and death.

literal: For the [thing] impossible of the law, in which it was weak through the flesh, God, having sent His own Son in likeness of flesh of sin and concerning sin, condemned the sin in the flesh,
prose: For what the law could not do, in that it was weak through the flesh, God did, by sending His own Son in the likeness of sinful flesh and as a sin offering, and condemned sin in the flesh,

literal: in order that the righteous-requirement of the law might be fulfilled in us, who walk not according to flesh but according to Spirit.
prose: so that the righteous requirement of the law might be fulfilled in us, who walk not according to the flesh but according to the Spirit.

literal: For the ones being according to flesh think the things of the flesh, but the ones according to spirit [think] the things of the spirit.
prose: For those who are according to the flesh think the things of the flesh, but those who are according to the spirit think the things of the spirit.

literal: For the mindset of the flesh [is] death, but the mindset of the Spirit [is] life and peace;
prose: For the mindset of the flesh is death, but the mindset of the Spirit is life and peace;

literal: Because the mind-set of the flesh [is] hostility toward God; for to the law of God it is not subjected, for neither is it able [to be];
prose: Because the mind of the flesh is hostility toward God, for it does not submit to the law of God, nor indeed can it;

literal: But those being in flesh are not able to please God.
prose: And those who are in the flesh cannot please God.

literal: If indeed [the] Spirit of God dwells in you. But if anyone [the] Spirit of Christ not has, this one not is of him.
prose: If indeed the Spirit of God dwells in you. But if anyone does not have the Spirit of Christ, he does not belong to him.

literal: But if Christ [is] in you, the body indeed [is] dead on account of sin, but the spirit [is] life on account of righteousness.
prose: But if Christ is in you, the body is dead because of sin, but the spirit is life because of righteousness.

literal: But if the Spirit of the one who raised Jesus out from among the dead dwells in you, the one who raised Christ Jesus out from among the dead will give life [also] to the mortal bodies of you through his Spirit that dwells in you.
prose: But if the Spirit of the one who raised Jesus from the dead dwells in you, the one who raised Christ Jesus from the dead will also give life to your mortal bodies through his Spirit that dwells in you.

literal: Therefore then, brothers, debtors we are, not to the flesh, to live according to the flesh,
prose: So then, brothers, we are debtors, not to the flesh, to live according to the flesh,

literal: For if according to the flesh you live, you are about to die, but if by [the] Spirit the deeds of the body you put to death, you will live.
prose: For if you live according to the flesh, you are about to die, but if by the Spirit you put to death the deeds of the body, you will live.

literal: For as many as by [the] Spirit of God are led, these sons of God are.
prose: For as many as are led by the Spirit of God, these are sons of God.

literal: For not you received a spirit of slavery again into fear, but you received a spirit of adoption, in which we cry, "Abba, the Father"
prose: For you did not receive a spirit of slavery, to fall back into fear, but you received a spirit of adoption, by which we cry, "Abba, Father!"

literal: Abba, the Father; the Spirit itself bears-witness-together with our spirit, that we are children of God.
prose: Abba, Father; the Spirit itself bears witness together with our spirit that we are children of God.

literal: And if children, also heirs: heirs on the one hand of God, and fellow-heirs of Christ, if indeed we suffer together, in order that we may also be glorified together.
prose: And if children, then also heirs: heirs of God, and fellow heirs with Christ, if indeed we suffer with him so that we may also be glorified with him.

literal: For I reckon that the sufferings of the now time [are] not worthy with-regard-to the about-to-be glory, for-it-to-be-revealed unto us.
prose: For I consider that the sufferings of the present time are not worthy to be compared with the glory that is about to be revealed to us.

literal: For the eager-expectation of the creation awaits the revelation of the sons of God.
prose: For the eager expectation of creation awaits the revelation of the sons of God.

literal: For to the futility the creation was subjected, not willingly, but on account of the one who subjected [it], in hope,
prose: For the creation was subjected to futility, not willingly, but because of him who subjected it, in hope,

literal: that also the creation itself will be freed from the slavery of the corruption into the freedom of the glory of the children of God.
prose: that the creation itself also will be set free from the slavery of corruption into the freedom of the glory of the children of God.

literal: For we know that all the creation groans-together and suffers-agony-together until the now.
prose: For we know that the whole creation groans together and suffers agony together until now.

literal: Not only [so], but also [we] ourselves, having the firstfruits of the Spirit, [we], we ourselves also, in ourselves groan, awaiting eagerly [the] adoption, the redemption of our body.
prose: Not only that, but we ourselves also, who have the firstfruits of the Spirit, we ourselves groan within ourselves, eagerly awaiting our adoption as sons, the redemption of our body.

literal: For in the hope we were saved. But hope being seen is not hope; for that which someone sees, why does he hope [for it]?
prose: For in hope we were saved. But hope that is seen is not hope; for why does one hope for what he sees?

literal: But if what we do not see we hope for, through patience we wait eagerly for [it].
prose: But if we hope for what we do not see, we wait for it eagerly through patience.

literal: For the what we should pray, as it is necessary, we do not know, but the Spirit himself intercedes with groanings inexpressible,
prose: For we do not know what we should pray for as we ought, but the Spirit himself intercedes with inexpressible groanings,
